title: Avoidance
wikitext:
'''Avoidance''' is a keyword used to describe several different chance-based forms of mitigation against [[hit]]s, certain types of [[damage]], or [[debuff]]s or other mechanics. __TOC__ ==Mechanics== Avoidance can be categorized into three major categories: hit avoidance, damage avoidance, and mechanic avoidance. ===Hit avoidance=== Hit avoidance currently is primarily against projectiles, typically worded as {{c|mod|#% chance to avoid Projectiles}}, which prevents a [[hit]]/collision from a projectile, causing it to pass through the target as if it were [[evasion|evaded]] or [[dodge|dodged]]. Hit avoidance prevents the hit entirely and will not trigger any on-hit/when-hit effects or [[projectile behaviour]]s or reduce remaining projectile behaviour counts (e.g. [[pierce]]). While worded similarly, {{c|mod|Avoid Projectiles that have Chained}} does not appear to be a conditional 100% chance to avoid projectiles: it does not prevent the collision. ===Damage avoidance=== Damage avoidance, typically worded as {{c|mod|#% chance to Avoid X Damage from Hits}}, is a form of [[receiving damage|damage mitigation]] against [[hit]]s that reduces the damage of certain [[damage type]]s to 0. It is considered preventing damage for stats like {{psl|Untiring}} or {{psl|Divine Shield}}. Avoiding all damage from hits does not prevent or undo the hit; on-hit/when-hit effects will still occur for both the attacker and defender. Avoidance should not be confused with [[evasion]], [[dodge]], [[block]], or [[immunity]] to damage. The chance to avoid damage from hits is hard capped at 75%.https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/2784310#characterbalance [[The_Forbidden_Sanctum#Resolve_defences|Resolve Avoidance]], a mechanic found exclusively in [[the Forbidden Sanctum]], functions similarly to damage avoidance; it does not prevent the hit, but will prevent all Resolve loss from the hit. ===Mechanic avoidance=== Mechanic avoidance is the most commonly found type of avoidance that applies to different types of [[debuff]]s or mechanical effects. Mechanic avoidance is most often used in the context of [[Ailment#Ailment defences|ailment avoidance]]. Stacking 100%+ chance to avoid X ailment is functionally identical to having the stat {{c|mod|Cannot be X-ed}}, although the inverse is not true for stats such as the one found on {{il|Stormshroud}}. This form of ailment defence is distinct from ailment immunity in that achieving 100% ailment avoidance will not remove any existing stacks of that ailment.https://i.imgur.com/GcAFB0I.png Ailment avoidance is absolute and will prevent the avoided ailment from being inflicted, even if the attacker has a 100% chance to inflict or "always" inflicts ailments - these chances are multiplicative against each other. Avoided ailments are not counted as inflicted by the attacker. 100% ailment avoidance against non-damaging ailments also prevents the corresponding type of [[ground effect]] from affecting the target ({{stl|Chilled Ground}}, {{stl|Shocked Ground}}, Scorched Ground, Brittle Ground, and Sapped Ground). This does not affect {{stl|Burning Ground}} and {{stl|Desecrated Ground}} as they are not considered [[ignite]] or [[poison]] respectively. Other forms of mechanic avoidance include chance to avoid {{stl|Blind}}, {{stl|Impale}}, [[knockback]], or [[stun]]. These follow the same rules as ailment avoidance. (The stun-specific {{c|mod|#% chance to Ignore Stuns}} stat is effectively avoidance, as it ignores stun for all purposes, though it is not additive with {{c|mod|#% chance to Avoid being Stunned}}.)
